drivingQuestion: Why is one credible to testify as an adult that a place is a beit haperas?
outcomeNote: credibility follows from the rabbinic status of beit haperas

segments.he: וְשֶׁהַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה בֵּית הַפְּרָס הוּא. מַאי טַעְמָא? בֵּית הַפְּרָס דְּרַבָּנַן. דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מְנַפֵּחַ אָדָם בֵּית הַפְּרָס וְהוֹלֵךְ. וְרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: בֵּית הַפְּרָס שֶׁנִּידַּשׁ — טָהוֹר. מַאי טַעְמָא — אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְעֶצֶם כִּשְׂעוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא נִידַּשׁ בָּרֶגֶל.
segments.en: «And» the mishna states that one is deemed credible to testify in his adulthood that as a minor he saw «that this place is a beit haperas.» The Gemara asks: «What is the reason» that he is deemed credible to testify what he witnessed as a minor? The Gemara answers: The ritual impurity of a «beit haperas» is «by rabbinic» law, «as Rav Yehuda said» that «Shmuel said: A person» who passes through «a beit haperas may blow» on the dust before taking each step, so that if there is a bone beneath the dust he will expose it, avoid it, «and proceed.» One may not rely on that method of examination with regard to impurity by Torah law. «And Rav Yehuda bar Ami, in the name of Rav Yehuda, said: A beit haperas that has been trodden» underfoot, creating a path, «is pure. What is the reason?» It is that «it is impossible for a bone» the size «of» a grain of «barley,» whose possible presence led to the decree of impurity, «not to have been trodden underfoot» and rendered smaller. This presumption is possible only in cases of impurity by rabbinic law.
